To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) DCNN feature representations contain information about the yaw, pitch, and image type of the face; (b) view-dependent coding is a characteristic of the individual identities, rather than the DCNNS; and (c) image quality information is encoded in the feature space, such that the center of the feature space is occupied by poor quality images.
the top-level DCNN features are highly informative about the identity of the face and the pose and quality of the image.

(1) the DCNN features contain surprisingly accurate information about face pose and image quality, (2) the view-dependent coding of faces is characteristic of the identities, and (3) the DCNN feature values are monotonically related to the quality of the face images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nature of the features learned by deep CNNs.
the nature of the feature-based face representation produced by deep CNNs.
the nature of face representation in deep neural networks, and the extent to which this representation can be leveraged to improve the performance of face recognition systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the face representations produced by DCNN feature extraction algorithms are highly robust to variations in viewpoint and appearance.
DCNN features are view-dependent, but the view dependence is a function of the identity rather than the DCNNS.
the top level features of DCNNs for face recognition are highly robust to changes of viewpoint, illumination, pose, expression, and appearance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DCNNs learn to encode face information in an extremely compact form, such that each feature is highly selective to a particular identity and/or face attribute.

the DCNNs have learned to represent the identity of the face in an abstract, invariant way, but they also have learned to represent a wide range of face metadata, including image quality and pose information, which is not necessarily identity-specific.
the face representations in deep CNN features are view-invariant for some identities, and view-dependent for others.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DCNNs used in recent face recognition algorithms are not only highly robust to changes of pose, expression, illumination, and other factors, but they also encode information about the identity and the image quality of a face in the top-level feature representations that are used to make recognition decisions.
face representations in DCNNs are not invariant to changes in pose or viewpoint, and that view-dependent coding of faces is a characteristic of the identity rather than the DCN.
the top-level DCNN features are surprisingly rich and contain a great deal of information about faces that is useful for face recognition.
